findings.claim: In V2, canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin with only an all-groups VIEW permission therefore passes requireManage(). That lets them create top-level groups and move any existing group to top level. The interface Javadoc (GroupPermissionEvaluator.java ~75) copies the same 'VIEW or MANAGE' wording.
findings.evidence: GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (GroupsResource.java:181) is guarded only by auth.groups().requireManage(). With rep.id set, it calls realm.moveGroup(child, null) (GroupsResource.java:198). canManage(GroupModel) at line 78 correctly requires MANAGE only, so the no-arg version looks like canView() copied into canManage(). In V1, canManage() means MANAGE_USERS only. testViewGroups grants VIEW but never attempts a write. Repro sketch, not run: createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(VIEW)), then groups().add(new GroupRepresentation named 'x'). Expected 403; the patched code returns 201.
findings.reason: All four seats raised it independently. Severity is normalised to Critical because view-only access becomes a write (privilege escalation). Every seat's claim is reasoned, not observed, and the gate did not run, so step 5 must first make the VIEW-only groups().add -> 403 test red. Fix canManage() to hasPermission(null, MANAGE) and correct the interface Javadoc in the same change.

findings.claim: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource UUIDs, not group IDs. It only ever evaluates the all-groups 'Groups' type resource. Result: (A) with all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS, GET /users and GET /users/count come back empty. (B) with only per-group VIEW_MEMBERS, the set is empty, so count returns 0 while search returns members through the post-filter, and pagination is applied before the canView post-filter, so pages come back short.
findings.evidence: Per-group resources are created untyped by resourceStore.create(server, name, owner) in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource. Only init() sets type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:271-274). findResourceIdByType filters on r.type = :type, so findByType(server, 'Groups') returns only the type resource. hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) calls findByName with a UUID, misses, and falls back to the type resource. Line 123 then adds the resource UUID. The set reaches UserModel.GROUPS at UsersResource.java:398/425/430/448 and BruteForceUsersResource.java:147. JpaUserProvider then filters on a non-existent group (lines 762-765, 1059-1089), and getUsersCount(realm, emptySet) returns 0 (JpaUserProvider.java:599-602). V1 adds resource.getName() minus the prefix (GroupPermissions.java:313-315). testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers passes only via the post-filter and never asserts count. Repro sketches, not run: all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS then users().search(null,-1,-1) expected to contain the member; per-group VIEW_MEMBERS on topGroup then users().count() expected 1.
findings.reason: All four seats raised it. Severity is normalised to Important: three seats rated it Important, superpowers rated it Critical. It is a functional break of search, count and paging, not an escalation. The claim is reasoned and unrun, so make it red first with both tests (all-groups search, per-group count). Ponytail's proposed fix (evaluate the Resource in hand and add groupResource.getName()) is insufficient on its own: the other three seats show that findByType never returns the untyped per-group resources, so the enumeration source must change too.

findings.claim: The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws when canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation checks canManageMembers.
findings.evidence: GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers (GroupPermissions.java:376-380) calls canManageMembers. The Javadoc was added in this patch.
findings.reason: Raised by all four seats. A doc-only correction, so no red test applies.

findings.claim: The Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says '@return Stream of IDs', but the method returns Set<String>.
findings.evidence: The return type is Set<String>. The Javadoc was added in this patch. Superpowers adds that it also omits the fact that V2 returns the type-resource ID (see the getGroupIdsWithViewPermission finding).
findings.reason: Three seats raised it. A doc-only correction; update it alongside the getGroupIdsWithViewPermission fix so the contract matches the corrected behaviour.

findings.claim: hasPermission evaluates either the per-group resource or the type resource, never both. Once any per-group resource exists for group G, for example another user's MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP on G, all-groups VIEW/MANAGE grants stop applying to G.
findings.evidence: DefaultPolicyEvaluator adds type-level policies only when resource.getType() != null, and per-group resources are untyped. findPolicyIdByNullResourceScope / findByScopes(server, null, ...) exclude policies tied to the type resource. The patch also removed the canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupsResource.java:113 and GroupResource getSubGroups, so listings depend on per-group canView. The same pattern pre-exists in UserPermissionsV2. Test sketch, not run: all-groups VIEW for myadmin plus per-group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP or VIEW_MEMBERS on topGroup for another user; groups().groups() / group(topGroup).toRepresentation() should succeed but are reasoned to return 403 or omit the group.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats, so not reported or fixed this loop. Severity stays Important and the claim is reasoned only (unverified). The check that would settle it is the mixed all-groups + per-group permission test above. It also overlaps with the patch's reliance on per-group canView after removing canViewGlobal.

findings.claim: A per-group grant leaks to every group that has no per-group resource. When the type resource is evaluated, findByResourceType pulls in every per-group permission, and the Groups copy of hasPermission lacks the permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()) filter that UserPermissionsV2 has.
findings.evidence: open-code-review: the type resource has type='Groups', so findByResourceType(server, 'Groups') (PolicyEntity.java:64) matches per-group permissions, and DecisionPermissionCollector.onComplete grants scopes without checking containsResource. ponytail: UserPermissionsV2 carries the resource-ID filter, added in c2acddc7ca to stop a single-user grant from granting all users; the Groups copy omits it without explanation. Test sketch, not run: per-group VIEW on myGroup for myadmin plus all-groups MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP for another user; groups().groups() expected size 1, reasoned to return 2.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Kept at Important as a potential authz leak, but unverified. Ponytail could not read c2acddc7ca and says exploitability was not proven, and open-code-review's claim rests on reading DefaultPolicyEvaluator, DecisionPermissionCollector and the JPA named queries. The settling check is the two-permission groups().groups() size test.

findings.claim: hasPermission is a third near-copy of the same evaluator, alongside UserPermissionsV2.java:94-133 and ClientPermissionsV2.java:207-235. It should be one shared hasPermission(resourceType, id, context, scopes...) on MgmtPermissionsV2.
findings.evidence: All three copies do the same steps: same-realm check, null server check, findByName, fall back to the type resource, evaluate, match scopes. The copies have already drifted (the resource-ID filter). Removing the duplication saves about 60 lines.
findings.reason: Appendix: one advisory seat. Advisory findings never block. The drift it points to is tracked in the per-group-grant leak finding.

findings.claim: The canView() Javadoc says 'Or if it has a permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups' without the 'For V2 only' qualifier that canList/canManage carry. V1 canView() checks roles only.
findings.evidence: Comparison of the Javadoc qualifiers on canView vs canList/canManage, against the V1 implementation.

findings.claim: Nothing cleans up V2 per-group FGAP resources and permissions when a group is deleted, so orphaned resources named after stale group IDs remain.
findings.evidence: The GroupRemovedEvent listener is registered only under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1). v1 and v2 share an unversioned feature key and are mutually exclusive. AuthorizationStoreFactory has synchronizers only for clients, realms and users. GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Reasoned and possibly planned for a later issue; the commit does not say.

findings.claim: The V1 feature check moved from event time to listener-registration time. In the legacy testsuite, V1 is enabled at runtime via @EnableFeature(skipRestart = true), so the role/client/group-removed cleanup listener never registers and V1 permission resources are orphaned in those runs.
findings.evidence: Runtime enablement in UsersTest.java:228/235/258/295 and the token-exchange tests. The seat concedes production is unaffected because Profile is fixed at boot.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat. Ponytail and superpowers say the refactor keeps the same behaviour because V1 and V2 are never on together, but that argument covers boot-time configuration only and does not address the skipRestart runtime-toggle case. The claim is therefore not disproven, and it remains reasoned and unverified.

findings.claim: The patch contains changes not related to the feature, against CONTRIBUTING.md ('No changes to code not directly related to your PR') and PR-CHECKLIST.md.
findings.evidence: Examples: the AdminPermissions listener restructure; ApiUtil.java:8-14 rewritten as try-with-resources; ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes removed (~176); UserPermissions canManageDefault/canViewDefault inlined (~229-299, 580-591), which forces a change in RolePermissions.java:302; AdminPermissionsSchema.java:54-76 constants reordered and if-chain replaced with a switch; GroupResource.java:206 'child = null' changed to 'child'; an unused import removed in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:32.
findings.reason: Appendix: one advisory seat. Ponytail and superpowers judged several of these deletions correct and behaviour-preserving, which does not bear on the scoping rule.

findings.claim: No documentation is included for the new 'Groups' resource type or the scopes manage-membership, manage-members and view-members.
findings.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md says 'Includes documentation' and PR-CHECKLIST.md requires documentation. fine-grain.adoc covers v1 only. v2 is EXPERIMENTAL, and the earlier Users/Clients v2 work is also undocumented.
findings.reason: Appendix: one advisory seat. Low severity given the EXPERIMENTAL status and precedent.

findings.claim: switch (resourceType) throws an NPE on a null resource type. Before the patch, a null type produced IllegalStateException('Could not map resource object...').
findings.evidence: updateResources (RepresentationToModel.java:1423) calls this for any admin-permissions policy with resources set. Only ScopePermissionRepresentation is validated to carry a resource type.

findings.claim: Realms whose admin-permissions client was initialised before this patch have no 'Groups' type resource and none of the new scopes. Group view/manage checks for admins without the MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles then return HTTP 500, and creating group permissions fails with 'Scope does not exist'.
findings.evidence: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early if the client already exists, and no migration is added. getResourceTypeResource returns null, then policyStore.findByResource(server, null) throws an NPE at JPAPolicyStore.java:215 (resource.getId()).
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat. Reasoned; the feature is EXPERIMENTAL.

findings.claim: getResourceName is not extended for GROUPS. Group permission resources render a null displayName, and the type resource has no 'All groups' label, unlike USERS.
findings.evidence: Resources are created with a name only. getResourceName is used by PolicyResourceService.java:218 when listing a permission's resources.

findings.claim: Coverage gaps in the new test: no test of all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS, users().count(), VIEW-only write attempts, or mixed all-groups and per-group permissions. testManageGroupMembership grants both user-side and group-side scopes and asserts only the positive case, so it does not show that the group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP check is enforced.
findings.evidence: Inspection of the test methods. The other seats noted the same gaps only inside their canManage and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission findings.
findings.reason: Appendix: one seat as a standalone finding. The red tests step 5 requires for the two main-list fixes will close the first three gaps. The testManageGroupMembership negative case remains open.
